The league said in a release it entered into a memorandum of understanding with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to designate Kalshi and Polymarket…
articles.body:
The NBA announced Monday it is partnering with prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket, as multiple states have sued those companies in an attempt to establish their regulatory authority over them.

The league said in a release it entered into a memorandum of understanding with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to designate Kalshi and Polymarket as its preferred prediction market exchanges.

Via the agreements, NBA-related markets on the two platforms will face “significant integrity protections,” including a ban on trading by league and team personnel and “information-sharing obligations relating to investigations and suspicious trading.”

Scott Kaufman-Ross, the NBA’s head of media distribution and partnerships, said the sport’s “integrity” is the league’s “top priority.”

Kaufman-Ross added, “As this category develops, we believe it is important to work constructively with regulators and operators to help ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place. These partnerships represent an important step in establishing a framework that creates new opportunities to engage our fans.”

CFTC Chair Michael Selig said in a release he was “pleased” the NBA signed the memorandum with his commission, noting the professional basketball league is following MLB and the NHL in partnering with Kalshi and Polymarket.

New Jersey officials last month asked the Supreme Court to weigh in the legal battle between prediction markets and states, which seek to regulate the platform — despite Selig arguing his commission has sole jurisdiction over them.

A bipartisan coalition of 39 states and the District of Columbia have backed New Jersey’s request , saying Kalshi and Polymarket are “wrong” from arguing the federal government has regulatory power over them.

Adam Silver, commissioner of the NBA, has sided with prediction markets, saying on CNBC’s “ Squawk Box ” earlier this month that having a “consistent policy nationally” is in his league’s “best interest.”

The NFL, on the other hand, urged the Supreme Court to take up New Jersey’s request and argued regulation of prediction markets should fall to the states. The country’s most popular sports league has partnerships with multiple sportsbooks , who face competition from prediction markets.

articles.title: Claude reportedly bypassed paywall to access Georgia voter data
articles.summary: The model reportedly bypassed a paywall to retrieve aggregate vote counts but didn’t access individual voter records.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Anthropic’s Claude AI model reportedly accessed publicly available Georgia election data without human authorization, raising fresh questions about AI security and human oversight ahead of the midterm elections.

The company told Axios Claude accessed aggregate vote counts as part of an internal statistics project, bypassing a paywall to retrieve information that Georgia typically makes available for a fee.

An Anthropic spokesperson told the outlet the model didn’t access the state’s voter registration system, retrieve individual voter records or alter any voting records.

According to The Guardian , Claude exploited a loophole in an older version of the Georgia agency’s website, which issued digital access tokens that allowed users to reach the data. The outlet reported that the model requested a token without being instructed to do so.

Anthropic said it has since implemented safeguards to prevent similar actions.

The company also notified the Georgia secretary of state’s office and the White House about the incident weeks ago, according to a source familiar with the matter who spoke to Axios. The source said administration officials urged Georgia officials to disclose the incident publicly sooner, but they didn’t act on those requests.

The disclosure comes amid broader concerns about AI agents taking actions without explicit human authorization, as developers work to advance their capabilities while maintaining appropriate safeguards.

The Trump administration has previously scrutinized Anthropic for how it handles AI-related disclosures. The Georgia incident adds another layer to the debate over how much autonomy advanced AI systems should have and how effectively their actions can be controlled.

articles.title: RFK Jr. extends MAHA push to hospital food

Speaking at a press conference hosted at the Corewell Health Lifestyle and Culinary Medicine Practice…
articles.body:
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced on Monday that over 250 hospitals have signed a pledge to serve healthier meals to patients, advancing his “ Make America Healthy Again ” (MAHA) agenda’s focus on treating food as medicine.

Speaking at a press conference hosted at the Corewell Health Lifestyle and Culinary Medicine Practice in Grand Rapids, Mich., Kennedy said he expects improvements in patient satisfaction, citing hospitals that have already launched similar changes.

“We expect that we’ve already seen good results on that from the changes in the hospital food at Tampa General, which was one of the first hospitals to actually change its menu,” said Kennedy. “They are looking — that hospital is looking on its own at at measuring actual health outcomes. We’re confident that that’s going to happen.”

Kennedy also announced that hospitals that sign the Make Hospital Food Healthier Pledge will receive a badge they can display on their websites.

The pledge calls on hospitals to “review the latest nutrition science and use evidence-based dietary practices to strengthen food service programs.” Changes involved in the pledge include limiting sugar-sweetened beverages and refined carbohydrates, along with increasing fiber-rich whole grains.

Tina Freese Decker, president and CEO of Corewell Health, said at the press conference that the types of meals patients receive under this pledge would vary.

“We really work with our physicians and nutritionists and clinicians to make sure that it’s as healthy as possible,” said Freese Decker. “We serve thousands of people every day, three times a day, plus our team members, and each meal is organized by what they need, what is going on with their life, their chronic illness, why they may be in the hospital, and so we really work to customize it.”
